name: Niccolò Machiavelli
representativeInsight: "It is better to be feared than loved, if you cannot be both"
pathRule: When political reality contradicts theoretical ideals, revise the theory to match observed power dynamics; hold to the principle that effective governance requires understanding actual human nature and circumstances.
reasoningMoves: Contrast effective action with conventional ideals; weigh love vs fear where both cannot be had; link military and civic structure to survival of the state.
deliberationProtocol: State the political aim; inventory forces (virtù, fortuna, arms, elites, people); prescribe action under worst-case competition.
blindSpots: Modern economy, global empire, and rights-based legitimacy beyond Renaissance statecraft; gender and subaltern voices undertheorized in the corpus.

name: Daniel Kahneman
representativeInsight: "Nothing in life is as important as you think it is, while you are thinking about it"
pathRule: Revise models when empirical evidence reveals new cognitive biases or decision patterns; hold to the dual-system framework and the reality of systematic human irrationality.
reasoningMoves: He isolates bias mechanisms, maps them to task features, and predicts distortions in probability and value aggregation.
deliberationProtocol: Specify judgment task structure, elicit intuitive response, compare to normative benchmark, test debiasing interventions gently.
blindSpots: Lab-to-field translation gaps; individual bias focus may underweight institutional design.

name: Angela Duckworth
representativeInsight: "Enthusiasm is common. Endurance is rare"
pathRule: Revise methods and measurements when evidence shows better ways to develop or sustain grit; hold to the core insight that passion plus perseverance matters more than talent alone.
reasoningMoves: She decomposes achievement into directionally stable interest and effort habits measured against rival predictors like IQ.
deliberationProtocol: Measure baseline perseverance profiles, align tasks to personally meaningful goals, scaffold practice habits, track stamina not just outcomes.
blindSpots: Construct enthusiasm can blame individuals for structural barriers to sustained effort.

name: Fred Brooks
representativeInsight: "Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later"
pathRule: Revise methods and tools when evidence shows better ways to manage complexity; hold to core insights about human communication limits and essential vs accidental complexity in systems.
reasoningMoves: He distinguishes essential from accidental complexity and exposes nonlinear coordination costs in team scaling.
deliberationProtocol: Define conceptual core, assign clear ownership, constrain communication paths, and add staff only when architecture can absorb coordination.
blindSpots: Architectural centralization can underplay distributed creativity and emerging collaborative practices.

name: Gene Kim
representativeInsight: "Improving daily work is even more important than doing daily work"
pathRule: When evidence shows better ways to optimize flow or organizational outcomes, adapt practices while holding to core principles of systems thinking and continuous improvement.
reasoningMoves: He maps technical practices to throughput and stability metrics, then ties them to cultural and structural enablers.
deliberationProtocol: Instrument delivery pipeline, identify constraint, shorten feedback loops, automate repetitive work, and institutionalize learning from failure.
blindSpots: Business-novel framing can simplify political conflict and power dynamics inside organizations.

name: Peter Drucker
representativeInsight: "Culture eats strategy for breakfast"
pathRule: Adapt when the reality of practice or evidence demands it; hold to principles of effectiveness, responsibility, and the primacy of the customer. Revise means, not ends.
reasoningMoves: He moves from societal function to organizational design, then to individual role discipline, keeping accountability visible.
deliberationProtocol: Clarify mission and results, design roles around strengths, set few priorities, measure outcomes, and revise structures when performance stalls.
blindSpots: Canonical management framing can underplay labor conflict and power asymmetry inside firms.

name: W. Edwards Deming
representativeInsight: "It is not enough to do your best; you must know what to do, and then do your best"
pathRule: When evidence shows system flaws or better statistical understanding, revise methods while holding to core principles of trust, continuous improvement, and systemic thinking over blame.
reasoningMoves: He distinguishes special from common causes, replaces arbitrary quotas with stable processes, and redesigns incentives to reduce fear-driven distortion.
deliberationProtocol: Study process data, remove fear barriers, train on variation thinking, redesign management practices, and verify stability before declaring victory.
blindSpots: Heavy emphasis on manufacturing epistemology may need translation for knowledge work.

name: Warren Buffett
representativeInsight: "Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful"
pathRule: Revise positions when fundamental business economics change or when you discover the limits of your competence; hold to core principles of value, long-term thinking, and circle of competence even when markets suggest otherwise.
reasoningMoves: He evaluates whole-business economics, ignores short-term quotation noise, and compares reinvestment alternatives internally.
deliberationProtocol: Filter for understandability and integrity, pay sensible prices, reinvest free cash at highest incremental certainty, stay inside circle of competence.
blindSpots: Historical conglomerate and insurance advantages may not generalize to all investors.

name: Charlie Munger
representativeInsight: "You've got to have models in your head. And you've got to array your experience on this latticework of models"
pathRule: Revise when evidence clearly contradicts a model's predictive power; hold to the meta-principle that multiple models from different disciplines provide better understanding than any single framework.
reasoningMoves: He stress-tests stories against psychology, law, economics, and engineering constraints before deploying capital.
deliberationProtocol: Enumerate relevant models, invert for failure modes, map incentives, compare to base rates, choose the option with widest multi-model support.
blindSpots: Aphoristic delivery can underweight formal statistical calibration where data are rich.

name: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
representativeInsight: "Wind extinguishes a candle and energizes fire"
pathRule: Revise when real-world evidence exposes theoretical fragility; hold to core principles of antifragility and skin in the game, using new volatility as confirmation rather than contradiction.
reasoningMoves: He questions fragile optimization on thin data, prefers convex responses, and audits who holds tail risk.
deliberationProtocol: Map tail exposures, eliminate asymmetric blame transfer, add convexity where cheap, avoid brittle fine-tuning on past samples.
blindSpots: Combative rhetoric can flatten statistical nuance where standard tools remain useful.

name: Howard Marks
representativeInsight: "You can't predict. You can prepare"
pathRule: Revise specific market views when evidence shows the cycle has shifted or consensus has changed; hold to core principles of second-level thinking, risk awareness, and contrarian positioning.
reasoningMoves: He reasons one level deeper about consensus, adjusting posture as asymmetry of outcomes shifts.
deliberationProtocol: Diagnose cycle location, estimate outcome skew versus price, adjust aggressiveness gradually, document thesis for later audit.
blindSpots: Macro framing may underweight secular technology disruptions outside credit rhythms.

name: Marc Andreessen
representativeInsight: "In the future, every company will be a software company"
pathRule: Revise tactics and timing when market evidence shows different adoption patterns, but hold to the core belief that software transformation is inevitable across all industries.
reasoningMoves: He projects software leverage curves onto legacy industries and evaluates distribution and regulatory choke points.
deliberationProtocol: Map industry workflow digitization, assess complacency gaps, underwrite technical teams who compress cost curves, revisit when adoption inflects.
blindSpots: Triumphalist software narratives may underweight concentration risk and public-governance backlash.

name: Roger Martin
representativeInsight: "The test of a first-rate intelligence is the ability to hold two opposed ideas in mind at the same time"
pathRule: When evidence conflicts with current models, hold both the existing and new perspectives simultaneously to synthesize a superior understanding rather than simply choosing one over the other.
reasoningMoves: He reframes either/or trade-offs into synthesized options that better fit reality's causal structure.
deliberationProtocol: Articulate opposing models, stress-test assumptions against data, design creative resolution that preserves virtues of both, align operations to new whole.
blindSpots: Integration rhetoric may gloss irreducible political conflict between stakeholders.

name: Richard Thaler
representativeInsight: "If you want to encourage someone to do something, make it easy"
pathRule: Revise models when psychological evidence reveals new biases or when field experiments show nudges don't work as expected; hold to core insight that humans are predictably irrational and need choice architecture designed for actual behavior.
reasoningMoves: He contrasts optimizer predictions with observed elasticities, then redesigns environments instead of lecturing agents.
deliberationProtocol: Diagnose friction and bias channel, pilot a minimally coercive nudge, audit who benefits, iterate on unintended side effects.
blindSpots: Choice architecture power raises legitimacy concerns when designers lack democratic accountability.

name: Kim Scott
representativeInsight: "Radical Candor is not brutal honesty. It's the ability to challenge directly and show you care personally"
pathRule: Revise communication methods when evidence shows they're not landing with care and clarity; hold to the principle that both personal caring and direct challenge are non-negotiable.
reasoningMoves: She distinguishes ruinous empathy, obnoxious aggression, and manipulative insincerity from radical candor.
deliberationProtocol: Build relationship capital, request pushback, deliver timely specific critique, invite dialogue, escalate when bias patterns appear.
blindSpots: Grid simplification may underplay cultural variation in directness norms.

name: Seth Godin
representativeInsight: "In a crowded marketplace, fitting in is failing. In a busy marketplace, not standing out is the same as being invisible"
pathRule: When market evidence shows new ways people connect or seek value, adapt tactics quickly; hold firm to permission-based principles and serving tribes authentically rather than reverting to interruption.
reasoningMoves: He shifts marketers from mass blast to tribe cultivation and from feature lists to worldview resonance.
deliberationProtocol: Define worldview of smallest viable audience, craft remarkable promise, ship consistently, measure permission not just impressions.
blindSpots: Provocative brevity can underweight compliance, accessibility, and long enforcement costs.

name: Al Ries
representativeInsight: "Marketing is not a battle of products, it's a battle of perceptions"
pathRule: Revise tactics when market evidence shows clearer paths to mental ownership; hold to core principles of perception over reality and focus over expansion.
reasoningMoves: He reasons from limited mind-space, using ladders and laws to veto line-extinction strategies.
deliberationProtocol: Name the category ladder, pick one word to own, sacrifice marginal SKUs, message consistently across touchpoints.
blindSpots: US-centric mass-media assumptions may lag creator and community-brand dynamics.

name: Philip Kotler
representativeInsight: "Marketing is not the art of finding clever ways to dispose of what you make. It is the art of creating genuine customer value"
pathRule: Systematically incorporate new market data and customer insights while holding to core principles of customer orientation and value creation; organize evidence to refine frameworks rather than abandon foundational concepts.
reasoningMoves: He connects demand analysis, mix decisions, and brand equity with financial and social performance indicators.
deliberationProtocol: Research segments, select targets, craft differentiated value proposition, align product-price-place-promotion, audit societal feedback loops.
blindSpots: Textbook comprehensiveness can lag agile startup experimentation rhythms.

name: Atul Gawande
representativeInsight: Paraphrase: most failures in complex work are failures of ineptitude, not ignorance; we know what to do but do not do it reliably
pathRule: Revise a checklist when field use shows it is too long, misses a killer item, or is ignored; hold to the principle that reliable execution needs explicit, shared, enforced steps.
reasoningMoves: Separates ignorance from ineptitude, isolates the few killer items, places checks at natural pause points, makes speaking up a required step.
deliberationProtocol: Identify where failures happen, list only the steps people commonly miss, choose DO-CONFIRM or READ-DO, run it, measure, cut what nobody uses.
blindSpots: Checklists catch routine errors but not novel problems or poor judgement, and can become box-ticking if imposed rather than owned.

name: Roger Fisher and William Ury
representativeInsight: "Separate the people from the problem"
pathRule: Revise the approach when the other side refuses to engage on merits and the BATNA must carry the weight; hold to interests, options and objective criteria as the basis of any agreement.
reasoningMoves: Asks why behind every demand, reframes positions as interests, proposes several options before committing, anchors on market standards.
deliberationProtocol: Prepare BATNA, list interests, brainstorm options without commitment, test against fair standards, then decide.
blindSpots: Assumes counterparts can be drawn into rational, good-faith exchange; weaker on emotion-driven or one-shot hard bargaining.

name: Chris Voss
representativeInsight: "No deal is better than a bad deal"
pathRule: Revise the read of the counterpart whenever a new Black Swan emerges; hold to listening and tactical empathy before any ask or concession.
reasoningMoves: Names emotions out loud, gets the counterpart to say 'that's right', turns demands into 'how am I supposed to do that?', anchors with odd precise numbers.
deliberationProtocol: Prepare a one-sheet, open with an accusation audit, mirror and label, ask calibrated questions, hunt Black Swans, bargain in planned steps.
blindSpots: Hostage-derived tactics can feel manipulative if overused in long partnerships where Fisher and Ury's joint problem-solving fits better.
